verdict.headline: Renewed US-Iran strikes and surging factory prices sharpen the September rate-hike knife
verdict.label: Step aside — high conviction: US-Iran resumes, Brent +3.2% to $90.91; ISM Mfg Aug 56.0 (Prices Paid 59.5 vs 53.2 prior); 10Y 4.79% new 20-mo high; 30Y ~5.27%, 3bps from trigger; NFP Fri +475K est.
verdict.horizon: Through September 4 NFP; hard posture reset after September 16 FOMC
verdict.rationale_short: Two overnight catalysts have materially upgraded the bear case without yet formally flipping the regime. First, US forces struck Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz — resuming active combat in the now six-month-old war — prompting Iranian missile responses against the UAE and Jordan; Brent crude surged 3.2% to $90.91, injecting a fresh energy-inflation impulse at the worst possible moment. Second, ISM Manufacturing for August printed 56.0 (consensus 54.5, prior 54.2), the strongest factory read since January 2019, with the Prices Paid sub-index surging to 59.5 from 53.2 — the sharpest single-month jump in nearly two years. The combination reads as stagflationary: manufacturing activity is booming, input costs are accelerating. Both catalysts arrived simultaneously on the first session of September, the month the Fed is most likely to hike. The 10-year yield has moved to 4.79%, a new 20-month high; the 30Y is estimated at ~5.27%, within 3bps of the 5.30% regime trigger. September 16 FOMC hike probability, which entered the week at ~67%, has moved above 75% on this morning's data. Canada's $19.9B retaliatory tariffs remain on calendar for September 8 — oil above $90 arriving ahead of that date stacks an energy inflation wave on top of tariff-driven import price pressures. ISM Manufacturing's Prices Paid surge (59.5) is itself a forward inflation signal that will flow into CPI readings over the coming 1-2 months. NFP Friday (+475K consensus) is now almost a moot gate for hike conviction: even a modest print (~300K) would not be soft enough to derail the September move given the oil spike and factory inflation data. BTC is holding $78,010 (range: $77,690-$79,257 today) with the $76,661 Aug 24 structural support intact; Bessent buyback program begins September 9. Equities are down ~0.5% (SPX) to ~1% (NDX) in premarket, but the damage could extend at the open if ISM Prices Paid drives a further repricing of the long end. Step-aside posture maintained at high conviction: the formal regime breach threshold (30Y daily close above 5.30%) has not yet been triggered, but the current trajectory — oil spike plus factory inflation plus a hot labor market — makes a close above 5.30% this week the base case, not the tail risk.

watchlist_mentions.note: Friday September 4, 8:30 AM ET: consensus +475K, unemployment 5.1%. Today's ISM Manufacturing beat (56.0) with Prices Paid surging to 59.5 raises the floor for what constitutes a 'soft' number — the bar for NFP to derail the September hike has moved meaningfully higher. Even a 300K print likely does not offset the oil + factory inflation combination. ADP Wednesday (private payrolls, consensus ~400K) is the directional preview; a beat would lock in the hike with near-certainty before Friday.

Brent crude at $90.91 (+3.2%) on US-Iran Larak Island strike resumption. Strait of Hormuz accounts for ~20% of global oil shipments; active combat in the waterway creates a persistent supply-disruption premium. The regime trigger for Brent is $94.00. At $90.91, Brent is $3.09 from trigger — the closest the regime risk indicator has been to activation. National gasoline average has been above $4/gallon every day in August. This energy cost channel is the most direct transmission mechanism from geopolitics to CPI; each $5 increase in Brent adds approximately 0.15-0.20pp to headline PCE over 3-6 months.

$78,010 on Crypto.com exchange at 12:04 UTC (-0.63% on the day). Day range: $77,690-$79,257. The $76,661 Aug 24 structural support remains intact — the named invalidation level from the prior setup. BTC touched $79,257 intraday (overnight Asia session) before retreating on the Iran risk-off wave. The Bessent buyback program begins September 9 (8 days), providing a structural demand backstop. Two consecutive daily closes above $80K remains the bull confirmation threshold. Current posture: hold long above $76,661 support; risk-off geopolitical shock creates downside pressure but programmatic buying backstop is approaching.

~$219.14 premarket (+1.0% from Friday's ~$217). The Friday sell-the-news reversal (-4.3%) from the Thursday earnings pop is partially recovering in premarket. The critical question: does NVDA hold above $220 structural support on the open or does the macro risk-off backdrop (oil, yields) overwhelm company-specific stabilization. A Tuesday close above $220 would signal the Friday reversal was a one-session distribution; a close below $210 would open the gap fill target and signal the AI infrastructure repricing is deepening. AVGO earnings (estimated September 4-5) is the next Blackwell production data point.

~$395-400 estimated (Friday close -9.2%). The 'AI competition' demand erosion narrative has not been walked back — no management comment, no analyst upgrade in four days. Monday's tape confirmed the read-across: CRM held its post-earnings premium while INTU-adjacent SaaS names showed sympathy selling. Today's ISM Manufacturing beat (56.0) is a net positive for enterprise software demand broadly but does nothing to address INTU's specific AI substitution risk to its tax and accounting automation products. JPMorgan's $331 PT remains the downside anchor. The SaaS AI fault line (AI-as-product vs. AI-as-substitute) is now a week into pricing; Tuesday's session determines whether the gap widens or closes.

~$263-265 estimated. The Salesforce/Intuit AI software bifurcation (AI-as-product vs. AI-as-substitute) enters its second week. CRM's post-earnings premium ($260+ support) has held; today's macro risk-off backdrop (oil, yields) is the first test of whether the multiple can survive a broadmarket drawdown. A CRM close above $260 amid an S&P down ~0.5% would validate the bifurcation thesis as sector-specific, not just index-beta.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y yield — 3bps from regime trigger; ISM Prices Paid surge pulls timeline forward
trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y enters Tuesday at ~5.27%, 3bps from the 5.30% regime trigger. Today's ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid (59.5 from 53.2) plus Brent crude at $90.91 represent two simultaneous inflation acceleration signals. The week-ahead event stack — ADP Wednesday, NFP Friday (+475K consensus), Canada tariffs September 8 — was already the most inflation-dense corridor since Jackson Hole; today's ISM and oil move have pre-validated the inflationary read. A daily close above 5.30% on the 30Y formally converts the step-aside posture to bearish. The oil spike alone — historical correlation suggests a 5% crude move adds ~3-5bps to the long end within 48 hours — makes Tuesday a plausible trigger date.
trade_setups.entry: Watch for 30Y daily close above 5.30% — formal regime trigger. Inverse: 30Y closes at or below 5.10% only if NFP prints sub-200K and oil reverses on a ceasefire announcement.
trade_setups.invalidation: US-Iran ceasefire announced (oil reverses below $85) AND NFP September 4 prints below 200K AND 30Y closes at or below 5.10%.
trade_setups.horizon: Through September 4 NFP; hard reset on September 16 FOMC outcome.

trade_setups.asset: Brent crude / energy sector — $90.91 with $94.00 regime trigger in view
trade_setups.thesis: Brent at $90.91 is the closest the regime risk indicator has been to its $94.00 trigger since the framework was established. The Strait of Hormuz conflict (20% of global oil shipments) creates a persistent supply-disruption premium that does not resolve on a single strike; prior conflict cycles in July and August showed Brent recovering to pre-strike levels within 3-5 sessions only when a ceasefire or de-escalation was announced. No ceasefire is in sight. Energy sector (XLE, CVX, XOM) is the direct beneficiary; simultaneously, airline (DAL, UAL), trucking (ODFL, SAIA), and chemical (LYB, HUN) names face margin compression on fuel costs.
trade_setups.entry: Long energy sector ETF (XLE) above $90.91 Brent; trail stop to $88.00 (prior resistance-now-support). Short margin-sensitive transportation names on any relief bounce.
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent closes back below $88.00 on ceasefire/de-escalation news.
trade_setups.horizon: Through geopolitical de-escalation or Brent hitting $94.00 regime trigger, whichever first.

trade_setups.asset: BTC — $76,661 support holds; Bessent bid T-minus 8 days
trade_setups.thesis: BTC's day range of $77,690-$79,257 shows the coin absorbed the Iran risk-off wave without breaching the $76,661 structural support. The Bessent Treasury buyback program begins September 9 — now 8 days away — providing a defined demand backstop. The risk-off geopolitical tape is the primary headwind; if the broader market continues selling into the open, BTC may retest $77,500-$78,000. A sustained break below $76,661 (daily close) is the exit signal. Two consecutive daily closes above $80K is the bull confirmation for an aggressive re-entry.
trade_setups.entry: Hold long above $76,661. Re-enter aggressively on two consecutive daily closes above $80K.

bear_case: The bear case now has a specific three-layer inflation stack and a narrowed fuse. Layer one: US-Iran military escalation has pushed Brent crude to $90.91, $3.09 from the $94.00 regime trigger. With the Strait of Hormuz conflict entering its seventh month and no ceasefire signal, the oil premium is structural rather than episodic. Layer two: ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid surged to 59.5 from 53.2 — the biggest single-month jump in nearly two years — signaling that input cost inflation is now running hot across the manufacturing base. This feeds into PPI and, with a 2-3 month lag, into CPI. Layer three: Canada's $19.9B retaliatory tariffs at 15-50% rates take effect September 8, seven days from now, adding import-price inflation on top of energy and manufacturing costs. The 30Y, now estimated at ~5.27%, is 3bps from the 5.30% regime trigger — the formal conversion point from step-aside to bearish. If NFP Friday September 4 prints above 400K (consensus +475K), the September 16 hike is near-certain, and the 30Y could pierce 5.30% on the NFP release itself. In the combined scenario — hot NFP + oil above $90 + Canada tariffs + 30Y trigger breach — the pathway to SPX 7,500-7,600 by September 16 FOMC sharpens materially. The additional bear amplifier that didn't exist in last week's setup: if NVDA fails to hold $220 on the open and the AI infrastructure repricing expands to a broader semiconductor sell-off (AMD, AMAT, LRCX), the tech weight alone could subtract another 1-2% from the S&P in the same window. Conversion from step-aside to outright bearish requires a 30Y close above 5.30% or an SPX close below 7,600 post-NFP.
